items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: But before Hip died Hip owned the famous door there about 25 years or so before he passed away three or four years ago.

ctx.x: lean times for us you know. It's been up and down. The paddock certainly doesn't it doesn't ever strike me that it does particularly good business.

No I guess the only reason the paddock survives is because they have a get these bus tours that come on the street which is a captive audience. You buy a ticket it'll take you to so many places and if that happens to be one of them you go there whether or not you're interested you see and whether or not you really appreciate the music. But that does seem to keep about three places alive on the street the 500 Club, the show bar and the paddock. The rest of them we must take our chances as they go by or they…
How is it that you get that somebody gets the tour and somebody else doesn't?
